Title: Case-control enrichment of a recurrent SCN5A missense variant in Brugada syndrome
Authors: A. Fictional, B. Placeholder (Institute of Demonstration Cardiogenetics)
Recruitment: 85 unrelated probands with a clinical diagnosis of Brugada syndrome were recruited
from a single arrhythmia referral center between 2016 and 2023. Diagnostic ajmaline challenge
testing was performed on all probands. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on all probands.

Target variant: NM_198056.3:c.5350G>A (p.Val1784Met)

CASE ENRICHMENT
The variant was identified in 9 unrelated probands in our Brugada syndrome cohort (9/85). It was
absent from 3,212 in-house control exomes from individuals without a personal or family history
of arrhythmia. Each of the 9 carriers was an independent proband from a distinct family; only the
proband was counted per family. The enrichment of this variant in cases versus controls was
statistically significant (p < 0.001).

No family members of any carrier were available for follow-up testing, so no segregation analysis
could be performed. No functional (electrophysiological) studies of this variant were undertaken
by this group or reported elsewhere. No RNA-based splicing study was performed for this variant.
Carriers presented with a range of arrhythmia phenotypes (syncope, documented VT, and asymptomatic
ECG findings on family screening for unrelated reasons); this phenotypic range is not considered
distinctive enough to be highly specific to SCN5A-related disease on its own.
demos.reasoning: The variant NM_198056.3:c.5350G>A is associated with Brugada syndrome, and the authors found a statistically significant enrichment of this variant in cases versus controls.

criteria.evidence: The variant was identified in 9 unrelated probands in our Brugada syndrome cohort (9/85) and was absent from 3,212 in-house control exomes from individuals without a personal or family history of arrhythmia. The enrichment of this variant in cases versus controls was statistically significant (p < 0.001).

Title: Cosegregation of an LMNA missense variant with autosomal dominant dilated cardiomyopathy
in a five-generation family
Authors: C. Example, D. Fictional (Northern Demonstration Cardiogenetics Group)
Recruitment: a single five-generation family with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and
conduction disease was ascertained through a proband referred for cardiac genetic testing.

Target variant: NM_170707.4:c.1130G>A (p.Arg377His)

SEGREGATION
The variant was tracked by Sanger sequencing across all available family members. It cosegregated
with clinically confirmed DCM and/or conduction disease in 8 affected relatives across three
generations, in addition to the proband. Two individuals were obligate carriers based on their
position in the pedigree (each has an affected parent and an affected child) and were counted as
carrying the variant without direct genetic confirmation. No genetically confirmed carrier over
age 40 was free of cardiac disease. This is an autosomal dominant pedigree with no consanguinity
and no history suggestive of recessive inheritance.

No case-control cohort was assembled for this variant, so no enrichment statistic is reported. No
functional studies of the variant were performed. No RNA-based splicing study was performed. The
proband's phenotype (DCM with conduction disease) is common to many cardiomyopathy genes and is
not considered specific enough to LMNA on its own to support a phenotype-specificity claim.
demos.reasoning: The paper provides evidence for cosegregation of the variant with disease in a five-generation family, but does not mention a second pathogenic variant in trans.

criteria.evidence: The variant was tracked by Sanger sequencing across all available family members. It cosegregated with clinically confirmed DCM and/or conduction disease in 8 affected relatives across three generations, in addition to the proband.
The proband's phenotype (DCM with conduction disease) is common to many cardiomyopathy genes and is not considered specific enough to LMNA on its own to support a phenotype-specificity claim.

Title: A novel PAH missense variant identified in trans with a known pathogenic variant in an
infant with phenylketonuria
Authors: E. Placeholder, F. Demonstration (Institute of Fictional Metabolic Genetics)
Recruitment: a single proband identified through newborn screening for phenylketonuria (PKU), a
well-established autosomal recessive metabolic disorder, followed by confirmatory biochemical and
molecular testing.

Target variant: NM_000277.3:c.1066-11G>A

TRANS CONFIGURATION
Molecular testing identified the target variant on one allele. Parental testing confirmed the
proband's mother carries the target variant and is otherwise unaffected. The proband's father was
found to carry the well-established pathogenic variant NM_000277.3:c.1222C>T (p.Arg408Trp), which
is one of the most common pathogenic PAH alleles and is absent in the mother. Segregation in the
family therefore confirms the target variant is in trans with (on the opposite chromosome from)
the known pathogenic c.1222C>T variant, consistent with the proband's autosomal recessive PKU
phenotype.

No case-control cohort was assembled for the target variant, so no enrichment statistic is
available. No functional assay of the target variant was performed. No RNA-based splicing study
was performed. Segregation data are limited to this single trio and do not constitute the kind of
multi-generation affected-relative cosegregation that would support PP1.
demos.reasoning: The paper describes a recessive gene with the target variant confirmed in trans with a separate, named, well-established pathogenic variant.

Title: Recurrent de novo SCN2A missense variant in three unrelated children with early-onset
developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
Authors: G. Fictional, H. Example (Center for Demonstration Pediatric Neurogenetics)
Recruitment: 3 unrelated probands with early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
were recruited via a pediatric neurogenetics clinic between 2019 and 2023. Trio (proband +
both biological parents) whole-exome sequencing was performed for all three families.

Target variant: NM_021007.3:c.2573G>A (p.Arg858Gln)

DE NOVO CONFIRMATION
The target variant was identified in all 3 probands. In each family, targeted Sanger sequencing
confirmed the variant was absent in both biological parents, and biological parentage was
confirmed by informative SNP analysis in all three trios. All three occurrences are therefore
independently confirmed de novo events. No parent in any family carried the variant, and none of
the parents reported a personal history of seizures or developmental delay.

No case-control cohort comparison was performed for this variant. No functional (electrophysiology)
studies were conducted. No RNA-based splicing study was performed. Phenotypes across the three
probands varied in severity and are not considered specific enough on their own, independent of
the de novo evidence, to support a phenotype-specificity claim.
demos.reasoning: The paper focuses on de novo occurrence of the variant NM_021007.3:c.2573G>A in three unrelated children with early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, and does not provide any additional evidence for other ACMG/AMP criteria.

criteria.evidence: The target variant was identified in all 3 probands, and in each family, targeted Sanger sequencing confirmed the variant was absent in both biological parents, and biological parentage was confirmed by informative SNP analysis in all three trios.

signature.instructions:
Apply the literature-DEPENDENT ACMG/AMP criteria to a variant by reading one
primary paper. Only use evidence the paper's authors explicitly report FOR THIS
VARIANT -- never assumptions, deductions, or work the paper merely cites.

Criteria:
- PS3: functional assay shows a damaging effect (needs wild-type AND null controls)
- PS4: case enrichment vs. controls (variant significantly more frequent in
  affected cases than in controls)
- PM3: ONLY for a recessive gene, where the target variant is found in trans
  (opposite chromosome copy) with a SEPARATE, independently-identified
  pathogenic variant in the same gene. The paper must name that second
  variant specifically. Do NOT apply PM3 just because the variant runs in a
  family or cosegregates with disease across relatives -- that is PP1, not
  PM3. If no distinct second pathogenic variant in trans is named, PM3 does
  not apply, no matter how large or multi-generation the family is.
- PS2_PM6: confirmed (PS2) or assumed (PM6) de novo occurrence
- PP1: cosegregation with disease across affected family members (the variant
  is tracked through relatives who are affected)
- PP4: phenotype highly specific to this gene / well-characterized workup
- PVS1_RNA: RNA study confirms a splicing loss-of-function effect

PP1 and PM3 are commonly confused: cosegregation or family-inheritance
evidence alone is PP1. PM3 requires a second, distinct pathogenic variant
in trans -- never infer PM3 from segregation data by itself.

If no literature-dependent criteria apply, return an empty list.
